messages.body_plain:
Dear Thiago, dear list,

we now have a basic AHM book website up and running:

www.mbr-pwrc.usgs.gov/pubanalysis/keryroylebook/ <http://www.mbr-pwrc.usgs.gov/pubanalysis/keryroylebook/>

You find everything that you need in terms of Supplementary Materials for volume 1 of the Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology book:

messages.subject: Dail-Madsen Model Convergence Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I hope everyone is enjoying the holidays.

I was writing for advice on running a Dail-Madsen Model. I can't get the D-M model to converge with simulated data in JAGS when the number of individuals per site, recruitment rate, and detection probability are low.

#------------------------ The model DOES converge with these parameters

# I am running 2 independent D-M models in the code- that's why everything has a 1 or 2.
# Later, I'd like to connect the 2 D-M models, but right now, they are completely separate
# The complete simulation code and model are at the bottom of this email

# Number of sites
M <- 199

# Number of repeated samples
T <- 10

# Average number of individuals per site
lambda1 <- 3
lambda2 <- 3

# Average recruitment rate
gamma1 <- 2
gamma2 <- 2

# Average survival rate
omega1 <- 0.9
omega2 <- 0.9

# Average detection probability
p1 <- 0.8
p2 <- 0.8

#------------------------ The model DOES  NOT converges with these parameters
# Number of sites
M <- 199

# Number of repeated samples
T <- 10

# Average number of individuals per site
lambda1 <- 1
lambda2 <- 1

# Average recruitment rate
gamma1 <- 1
gamma2 <- 1

# Average survival rate
omega1 <- 0.9
omega2 <- 0.9

# Average detection probability
p1 <- 0.3
p2 <- 0.3

#---------- Things I've tried to improve convergence:

(1) Providing realistic initial values (see code below)

(2) Running the model for 1 million iterations, with a burn-in of 100,000, and thinned by 1,000 (3 chains)
#this was the output:

> summary(output2)
JAGS output for model 'model.txt', generated by jagsUI.
Estimates based on 3 chains of 1e+06 iterations,
burn-in = 1e+05 iterations and thin rate = 1000,
yielding 2700 total samples from the joint posterior.
MCMC ran in parallel for 1063.134 minutes at time 2015-12-24 00:19:39.

              mean      sd      2.5%       50%     97.5% overlap0 f  Rhat n.eff
lambda1    931.133 558.695    98.696   969.066  2118.577    FALSE 1 1.110    36
lambda2    589.446 458.441   105.828   400.983  1715.840    FALSE 1 2.342     4
omega1       0.992   0.014     0.936     0.997     1.000    FALSE 1 1.343    21
omega2       0.970   0.033     0.894     0.986     1.000    FALSE 1 1.598     7
p1           0.001   0.001     0.000     0.001     0.005    FALSE 1 1.015   234
p2           0.001   0.001     0.000     0.001     0.004    FALSE 1 1.138    19
gamma1     149.029  75.348    33.405   142.132   366.895    FALSE 1 1.244    21
gamma2     170.846  91.273    45.020   144.270   352.946    FALSE 1 1.031   136
deviance 11121.549  95.467 10955.422 11112.264 11288.132    FALSE 1 1.584     7

**WARNING** Rhat values indicate convergence failure.
Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor (at convergence, Rhat=1).
For each parameter, n.eff is a crude measure of effective sample size.

overlap0 checks if 0 falls in the parameter's 95% credible interval.
f is the proportion of the posterior with the same sign as the mean;
i.e., our confidence that the parameter is positive or negative.

DIC info: (pD = var(deviance)/2)
pD = 3005.6 and DIC = 14127.16
DIC is an estimate of expected predictive error (lower is better).

My Questions:

(1) Has anyone had similar experience?

(2) Any suggestions on how to make the D-M model converge?

(3) Even more confusing is that my data (which has very low counts- and likely has small parameter estimates)- fits well using unmarked. Has anyone else seen this?

Sorry for the long email! And THANK YOU for any input!!! I really appreciate your time.
Best wishes,
Grace

#------------------------------- Here is the code for the simulated data and the model
# Number of sites
M <- 199
# Number of repeated samples
T <- 10
# Average number of hosts per site
lambda1 <- 1
lambda2 <- 1

# Average recruitment rate
gamma1 <- 1
gamma2 <- 1

# Average survival rate
omega1 <- 0.9
omega2 <- 0.9

# Average detection probability
p1 <- 0.3
p2 <- 0.3

# Days
days <- matrix(1, nrow = M, ncol = T)

# Data matrix + true number of hosts
y1 <- N1 <- matrix(NA, M, T)
y2 <- N2 <- matrix(NA, M, T)

# Survival + recruitment matrix
S1 <- G1 <- matrix(NA, M, T-1)
S2 <- G2 <- matrix(NA, M, T-1)

# First year= poisson process
N1[,1] <- rpois(M, lambda1)
N2[,1] <- rpois(M, lambda2)

# Second + years; survival + recruitment = abundance
for(t in 1:(T-1)) {
  S1[,t] <- rbinom(M, N1[,t], omega1^days[,t])
  S2[,t] <- rbinom(M, N2[,t], omega2^days[,t])
  # Discrete probability distribution describing the number of sucesses in a sequence of independent events, each with a probability p of sucess
  G1[,t] <- rpois(M, gamma1 * days[,t])
  G2[,t] <- rpois(M, gamma2 * days[,t])
  # Discrete probability distribution describing the probability of a given number of events occurring in a fixed time interval if the events have an average rate + are idendentent of the time since last event
  N1[,t+1] <- S1[,t] + G1[,t]
  N2[,t+1] <- S2[,t] + G2[,t]
  # Total abundance[next year] = survivors [last sampling] + gains[since last sampling]
}

y1[] <- rbinom(M*T, N1, p1)
y2[] <- rbinom(M*T, N2, p2)

sink("model.txt")
cat("
model{

#------------ Priors

    # Initial abundance
    lambda1 ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
    lambda2 ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)

    # Immigration rates
    gamma1 ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
    gamma2 ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)

    # Annual survivorship
    omega1 ~ dunif(0, 1)
    omega2 ~ dunif(0, 1)

    # Detection probability
    p1 ~ dunif(0, 1)
    p2 ~ dunif(0, 1)

#------------ Likelihood model

for(j in 1:nSites){

# Year 1

    N[j, 1, 1] ~ dpois(lambda1)
    N[j, 1, 2] ~ dpois(lambda2)

# Specify the model for years 2 through nYears

    for(t in 2:nReps){

# Estimate Survivorship

    S[j, t-1, 1] ~ dbin(omega1^days[j,t], N[j, t-1, 1])
    S[j, t-1, 2] ~ dbin(omega2^days[j,t], N[j, t-1, 2])

# Estimate recruitment
    G[j, t-1, 1] ~ dpois(gamma1 * days[j,t])
    G[j, t-1, 2] ~ dpois(gamma2 * days[j,t])

# Sum to get total N at location j in year t

    N[j, t, 1] <- S[j, t-1, 1] + G[j, t-1, 1]
    N[j, t, 2] <- S[j, t-1, 2] + G[j, t-1, 2]

    } #ts

 } # js

for(j in 1:nSites){
  for(t in 1:nReps){

    n[j, t, 1] ~ dbin(p1, N[j, t, 1])
    n[j, t, 2] ~ dbin(p2, N[j, t, 2])

  }
}

}

    ", fill = TRUE)
sink()

#--------------------------- MCMC settings
ni <- 1000000
nb <- 100000
nt <- 1000
nc <- 3

#--------------------------- Bundle the data

y <- Ni <- array(NA, dim = c(M, T, 2))

y[,,1] <- y1
y[,,2] <- y2

win.data <- list(nSites = M, nReps = T,
                 n = y, days = days)

#--------------------------- Initial values

Si <- Gi <- array(NA, dim = c(M, T-1, 2))

Ni[,,1] <- y1+1
Ni[,,2] <- y2+1

Si[] <- 1
Gi <- Ni[,-1,] - Si

Ni[ ,-1, ] <- NA

inits <- function(){
  list(
    omega1 = 0.9,
    omega2 = 0.9,
    p1 = 0.3,
    p2 = 0.3,
    gamma1 = 1,
    gamma2 = 1,
    lambda1 = 1,
    lambda2 = 1,
    N = Ni,
    S = Si,
    G = Gi
  )
}

#--------------------------- Parameters to monitor

params <- c("lambda1", "lambda2",
            "omega1","omega2",
            "p1","p2",
            "gamma1", "gamma2")

#--------------------------- Run the model
library("jagsUI")

output2 <- jags(win.data, inits, params, "model.txt",
                n.chains = nc, n.thin = nt, n.iter = ni,
                n.burnin = nb, parallel = TRUE)

summary(output2)

messages.subject: Re: Dail-Madsen Model Convergence Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi Grace,

What does your unmarked output look like?  Most folks find these models to be pretty unstable, particularly with low detection probabilities, small population sizes, and no secondary sampling replication.  With p=0.3 and lambda=1 there is very little information in those data, particularly for estimating both omega and gamma.  You might have better luck using a formulation where only a single dynamics parameter, the finite rate of increase, is estimated (as described in the unmarked pcountOpen help file).  I have not had much success with the DM model in JAGS, but I haven't worked with simulated data.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for the reply!

To test some ideas out, I fitted some models in unmarked using "disease status" simply as a covariate, with the counts for the two classes "stacked". i.e., I fit a model like:

 ~ status, ~ status, ~status, ~status

 and various simplifications for the 4 parameters.

 I fit this model to a data set with K = 4 sample occasions for one season (sampling occasions separated by a week or so, lets say).  NO REPLICATION.

 So the full model has lambda, omega, gamma, p, all depending on status -- 8 total parameters seems to converge but the SE is huge for a couple of the parameters. I guess it makes sense maybe some of them are poorly identified.

 So I fit a simpler model with gammaUninfected = gammaInfected (any simplification seems to work better)..

 CHECK THIS OUT:

Call:
pcountOpen(lambdaformula = ~status2, gammaformula = ~1, omegaformula = ~status2,
    pformula = ~status2, data = umf4, K = 100)

Abundance:
            Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)     0.25 0.342  0.73   0.465
status2        -1.01 0.686 -1.47   0.142

Recruitment:
 Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
    -1.16 0.344 -3.38 0.000716

Apparent Survival:
            Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    0.807 0.758  1.065   0.287
status2       -4.675 9.441 -0.495   0.620

Detection:
            Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)   -0.893 0.506 -1.765  0.0775
status2       -0.403 0.875 -0.461  0.6449

AIC: 1631.778

So the model seems to fit in unmarked well, with NO REPLICATION, and it indicates things that might make sense: (1) survival is lower (very low) for infected individuals but very high for uninfected.
In any case, the model seems to fit adequately and the solution looks like a stable solution (and most of the models below the full model look ok).

Next, here is the output from the JAGS independence model given at the end of the email. You see this is (1) not mixing at all; (2) and therefore shares no resemblance to the unmarked output....  in particular look at the estimated lambda1 and lambda2!

for(j in 1:nSites){

    # Year 1

    N[j, 1, 2] ~ dpois(lambda2)

With p=0.3 and lambda=1 there is very little information in those data, particularly for estimating both omega and gamma.  You might have better luck using a formulation where only a single dynamics parameter, the finite rate of increase, is estimated (as described in the unmarked pcountOpen help file).  I have not had much success with the DM model in JAGS, but I haven't worked with simulated data.

 I can answer that since I did the unmarked analysis for Grace. The model that is directly equivalent to the model she gave in JAGS is model 7 in the table which is specified in unmarked like this (status2 is a binary variable of disease status):
